This program is intended to meet the spirit and intent of the following regulations:
- California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2
- Federal EPA Risk Management Program (RMP)  Title 40 CFR §68
- California Process Safety Management (PSM) Program  Title 8 CCR §5189
- Federal Process Safety Management (PSM) Program  Title 29 CFR §1910.119

Hereafter this program will be referred to as the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program.

This program is intended to be a living document. As such, the information, procedures, policies, and documentation that make up this program must be made easily accessible and updated as necessary. To accomplish this, Jireh Packing Company has elected to use PSMWriter, software developed and distributed by Resource Compliance, Inc. This software will assist us with updating, maintaining, scheduling, and tracking RMP/PSM/CalARP related activities. 

1.1 Jireh Packing Company, Risk and Process Safety Management Program

This is to inform all interested persons, including employees, that Jireh Packing Company has developed their unified RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. This program has been prepared to address the risks involved in operating and maintaining the following processes which have the presence of hazardous chemicals above threshold quantities: 
Process Name                            | Process Chemical                        | Process Quantity(lbs.)
P1 South System                         Anhydrous Ammonia                    39,000
P2 East System                             Anhydrous Ammonia                    12,000

Our RMP/PSM/CalARP Program promotes overall plant, worker, public, and environmental safety. The program enables our facility to prevent the occurrence, and minimize the consequences, of significant releases of hazardous chemicals. Overall, the program is designed to prevent accidental fatalities, injuries, illnesses, and physical property damage.

Our company has many policies and procedu

res in place to promote overall plant, worker and public safety. We have: 
Prepared a unified program based on the PSM regulation to meet CalARP and RMP obligations as well
Organized the program so that it meshes closely with general business practices
Utilized PSMWriter software to ensure that all necessary employees have access to relevant information (SOPs, PHAs, audits, etc.)

The RMP/PSM/CalARP Program sets forth rules, procedures, and practices that will help our employees and neighbors protect themselves.

1.2 Process Descriptions

1.2.1 Facility Overview

Jireh Packing Company operates a commercial cold storage for stone fruit and citrus in Cutler, CA. The facility has two ammonia refrigeration systems that provide refrigeration capacity to the following:
P1 (South)
(9) Cold Storage Rooms
(2) Precool Rooms
(2) Conditioning Rooms
(3) Hallways
(1) Loading Dock
(1) Glycol Heat Exchanger

P2 (East)
(10) Bin Rooms

1.2.6 Process Classification
Each ammonia refrigeration system at Jireh Packing Company consists of vessels, equipment, and valves which are interconnected by piping. The systems are neither interconnected nor co-located relative to each other. As such, the refrigeration systems at Jireh Packing Company are treated as two (2) independent processes.
1.3 General Accident Release & Chemical Specific Prevention Steps
1.3.1 General 
We inform our employees engaged in process operations of the dangers of an accidental release of anhydrous ammonia in annual safety meetings. During these meetings we also discuss preventative measures, such as evacuation, in order to be prepared for a release.
Jireh Packing Company has also conducted an off-site consequence analysis of worst-case and alternative release scenarios for the ammonia refrigeration processes. These are for the purposes of informing the public in the event of an accidental release. The results of the analyses are reported in PSMWriter and hard copy binders. 
1.3.2 Anhydrous Ammonia
The ammonia refrige

ration processes at the Jireh Packing Company facility is an integral part of the overall business and operates most of the year. It is extremely important that this process is maintained and operated in a safe and efficient manner. Management is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of an ammonia leak.
Our refrigeration personnel monitor the ammonia refrigeration processes and keep active records of all procedures and transactions that pertain to ammonia. In addition, the process is checked frequently by one of the outside refrigeration contractors that we use. These contractors also assist in performing the annual mechanical integrity inspection of our ammonia equipment. 
1.4 Five Year Accident History
Jireh Packing Company has had no accidental release within the last five (5) years.
1.5 Emergency Action and Response Plan
Jireh Packing Companys emergency action and response program has been developed to satisfy the following requirements:
Cal/OSHAs Emergency Action Plan  Title 8 CCR §3220
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Emergency Action Plans  Title 29 CFR §1910.38
Cal/OSHAs Process Safety Management [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 8 CCR §5189(n)
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Process Safety Management [Emergency Planning and Response Requirements]  Title 29 CFR §1910.119(n)
California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2 §5120.1-5120.2
USEPA Risk Management Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 40 CFR §68.90-96
California Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) [Emergency Response Plans and Procedures]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 1 §5030.7
California Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER)  Title 8 CCR Title 8 §5192(q)
Federal Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER)  Title 29 CF

R §1910.120(q)

Strategically, Jireh Packing Company has chosen to be a non-responding stationary source. Our employees will not respond to accidental releases of ammonia. In lieu of responding to accidental releases, Jireh Packing Company is implementing the following protocols:
The facility is included in the community emergency response plan developed under Title 42 USC §11003.

Since the only regulated chemicals at the facility are flammable substances, Jireh Packing Company coordinates emergency response actions with the local fire department. 
Appropriate mechanisms are in place to notify emergency responders when there is a need for a response.

Annual emergency response coordination activities are performed (Section 1.5.1).
Annual notification exercises are performed (Section 1.5.2).

1.5.1 Emergency Response Coordination Activities

The purpose of emergency response coordination activities is to coordinate response needs with local emergency planning and response organizations. The intent is for local response organizations to be made aware of the regulated substances at Jireh Packing Company, their quantities, the risks presented by the covered processes, and the resources and capabilities at our facility to respond to an accidental release of a regulated substance. The emergency response coordination activities will consist of the following:
Coordinations will be completed at least annually. Additional coordinations will be made to account for changes at our facility that may affect the community emergency response plan.
Coordinations will include Jireh Packing Companys emergency response plan, updated emergency contact information, and any other information necessary for developing and implementing the local emergency response plan.

Coordination activities will be appropriately documented. The coordination records will include the names of individuals involved and their contact information (phone number, email address, and organizational affiliations),

dates of coordination activities, and nature of coordination activities.

The disclosure of information classified or restricted by the Department of Defense or other Federal agencies or contractors of such agencies is controlled by applicable laws, regulations, or executive orders concerning the release of that classified or restricted information.

1.5.2 Emergency Response Notification Exercises

At least once per calendar year, Jireh Packing Company will conduct an exercise of the facilitys emergency response notifications mechanism. The facility will record each notification exercise utilizing PSMWriter.

Alternatively, the facility may meet the notification requirements through other exercises conducted to meet other Federal, state or local requirements, provided that the necessary notification is performed. Additionally, if a notification is made in response to an accidental release, this would also satisfy the notification requirement.

1.6 Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Jireh Packing Company has implemented many policies and procedures to promote overall plant, worker, public, and environmental safety. Nevertheless, Jireh Packing Company continually strives to improve in all areas, including safety.

By utilizing PSMWriter software, all necessary employees have access to every aspect of the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. This has improved Jireh Packing Companys ability to communicate hazardous situations to employees and contractors. In addition, PSMWriter tracks all RMP/PSM/CalARP related events so that Jireh Packing Companys management team can ensure that the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program is being implemented.

Jireh Packing Company has implemented all aspects of the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. When a RMP/PSM/CalARP Program requirement is completed (i.e. mechanical integrity inspection, process hazard analysis, compliance audit, etc.) any specific action items related to that event are entered into PSMWriter, assigned a responsible person, and given a due date. Onc

e the action item has been completed, the resolution can be documented using PSMWriter as well. A list of current or past due action items can be accessed at any time by those with access to PSMWriter.

In addition to utilizing PSMWriter to create, schedule, track, and document events, Jireh Packing Company has also entered into a contract with Resource Compliance to obtain help with RMP/PSM/CalARP Program implementation.

Jireh Packing Company considers the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program a living document. It is an interactive framework that guides safe action for Jireh Packing Company employees, but allows for feedback and continual improvement. Through the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program Jireh Packing Company will continue to maintain overall plant worker, public, and environmental safety.
